notebooks.title: Linear Representation Hypothesis
notebooks.overview: Features correspond to directions $\phi \in \mathbb{R}^d$ in activation space. The projection $\phi^\top h_l(x)$ approximately measures the intensity of that feature for input $x$, and features combine additively: $h_l(x) \approx \sum_i \alpha_i \phi_i$. notebooks.title: Superposition Hypothesis
notebooks.overview: Model hidden states encode more features than they have dimensions. If there are $k$ features and $d$ dimensions with $k >> d$, models tend to reduce interference between features by representing them as nearly-orthogonal directions.

notebooks.title: Activation Oracles: Training LLMs to Explain Their Own Activations
notebooks.survey_reference: Section 8.5 - LatentQA and Activation Oracles ([Karvonen et al., 2025](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.15674))
notebooks.overview: **Activation Oracles** (AOs) are LLMs fine-tuned to accept another model's internal activation vectors as input and answer arbitrary natural-language questions about them. They build directly on **LatentQA** ([Pan et al., 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.08686)), which formulates representation decoding as a supervised learning problem: given a cached hidden representation $h^l_t$, a question $q$, and an answer $a$, we fine-tune a decoder on $(h^l_t, q, a)$ triplets via **Latent Interpretation Tuning** (LIT).
learning_objectives: Understand what Activation Oracles are and how they differ from patchscopes, probes, and SAEs
Use a pre-trained oracle to query model internals at token, segment, and sequence level
Implement the full oracle pipeline from scratch: activation extraction, placeholder tokens, steering hooks
Extract secret words from models fine-tuned to hide them (taboo task)
Use model-diffing (activation differences) to detect what fine-tuning changed
Evaluate oracle reliability across layers, prompts, and input types
